sections.title: Sound of S
paragraphs: The letter (S) /ʒ/ makes its main sound in (sun) /sʌn/, which means the bright star in the sky. This letter has three different sounds, and it can also be silent.

sections.title: How to say S
paragraphs: For the first sound, place your tongue near the ridge behind your upper teeth. Blow air through the narrow gap without voice. For the second sound, make that same hiss and turn your voice on. For the third sound, pull your tongue slightly further back, round your lips, and keep your voice on. Touch your throat to feel it shake when you add your voice.

sections.title: Spelling rules for S
paragraphs: At the start of words, the letter sounds like (sit) /sɪt/. Between two vowels or at the end of many words, it sounds like (rose) /roʊz/. Before the endings ion or ual after a vowel, it sounds like (vision) /vɪ.ʒən/. In some special words, you do not pronounce this letter at all, as in (island) /aɪ.lənd/.

sections.title: Common mistakes with S
paragraphs: Do not turn the sound in (busy) /bɪ.zi/ into a voiceless hiss. Many learners keep their voice turned off where English needs voice. Press your fingers against your throat to feel it buzz on the middle consonant. Do not say a consonant sound when the letter is silent, such as in (aisle) /aɪl/.
